title: Slow androgenetic hair loss and produce regrowth with approved medicines

concept.text: Modify common pattern hair loss pharmacologically, increasing or maintaining visible scalp hair during treatment. Finasteride and topical minoxidil established this capability; they do not create a new supply of follicles. Proposed completion test: FDA approval for androgenetic alopecia supported by controlled human trials showing improved target-area hair counts and photographic or patient assessments over approximately one year. Test set by: FDA; Propecia's pivotal programme used hair counts, standardized photographs and patient/investigator assessments. Reported achieved: FDA approved finasteride 1 mg (Propecia) for male pattern hair loss on 19 December 1997; topical minoxidil was already an established treatment. Sources given: [FDA confirmation of Propecia approval date](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/human-drug-compounding/fda-alerts-health-care-providers-compounders-and-consumers-potential-risks-associated-compounded) ; [Propecia clinical evidence and prescribing information](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=9e7329eb-39f1-4f84-a0bb-91daffaba1c3&type=display) ; [Topical minoxidil women's hair-regrowth label](https://dailymed.awsprod.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=c3ba93d7-e826-f6ac-e053-2a95a90a7951).

page.title: First approved medicines for androgenetic alopecia
page.definition: A medicine is approved for androgenetic alopecia, the progressive loss of scalp hair in a characteristic pattern, after controlled trials show more hair in a target area of scalp than with placebo. Topical minoxidil and oral finasteride are the first. They slow loss and increase hair count during use; they form no new follicles, and the benefit is lost when treatment stops.

goal.need: A 2001 clinic study examined 377 women aged 18–99 years for female pattern hair loss; its age-specific frequencies appear below. Progression is measurable in men: in two finasteride studies enrolling 1,553 men, 58% of placebo recipients had further target-area hair loss at 12 months.

statements.quote: Patients are looking for effective hair loss treatments to prevent further thinning and optimally stimulate regrowth.
Treatment can prevent hair loss from worsening and help women regrow their hair.
statements.context: The passage concerns female pattern hair loss.

completion.title: FDA approves a medicine indicated for androgenetic alopecia in men or in women.
completion.criterion: FDA approves a new drug application, or a supplement to one, for a medicine whose labelled indication is androgenetic alopecia (male or female pattern hair loss) in the case's population. The approval rests on randomized, double-blind trials in that population, controlled with placebo or vehicle, in which hair count in a defined target area of scalp is greater with the medicine than with control. The first such approval in each population meets the test for it. Compounded products and use outside an approved indication do not count. The test does not require earlier hair density restored, new follicles, or benefit that lasts after treatment stops.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, approved labelling: the prescribing information for Propecia (finasteride 1 mg), sections 1 and 14, states the indication, population and endpoints for men; the approval letter for NDA 021812/S-009 states the indication for women.
completion.threshold_quote: indicated for the treatment of male pattern hair loss (androgenetic alopecia) in MEN ONLY
completion.basis: The test is the regulator's first approval in each population. No regulator or society sets a minimum gain in hair count, so the test sets none. In the finasteride trials the primary endpoints were hair count and patient self-assessment; at 12 months the difference from placebo was 107 hairs in a 5.1 cm² circle, and the label states that stopping treatment reverses the effect within 12 months. Drugs@FDA records the original approval of topical minoxidil solution, NDA 019501, on 17 August 1988. Regeneration of new follicles is a separate entry, HLT-18.

milestones.title: Nonclinical evidence supports reasonably safe human testing of a candidate hair-loss medicine.
milestones.criterion: Pharmacology and toxicology studies, in animals or in vitro, show an effect of the candidate medicine on hair follicles and support the conclusion that the proposed human investigation is reasonably safe, as an investigational new drug application requires; the tests needed depend on the nature and duration of the investigation. Follicle pharmacology without toxicology, or toxicology without follicle pharmacology, is partial.
milestones.set_by: FDA, 21 CFR 312.23(a)(8), the pharmacology and toxicology requirement for an investigational new drug application.
milestones.threshold_quote: it is reasonably safe to conduct the proposed clinical investigations.

milestones.title: A candidate hair-loss medicine reaches human administration in clinical research.
milestones.criterion: The candidate medicine is given to people of the case's population in monitored clinical research that reports the dose, the number of people treated and the adverse events observed. The report need not describe the first exposure in that population.
milestones.set_by: FDA, Drug Development and Review Definitions, initial human testing under Phase I Clinical Studies.
milestones.threshold_quote: Phase 1 includes the initial introduction of an investigational new drug into humans.

milestones.title: Controlled studies provide preliminary evidence that a medicine treats pattern hair loss.
milestones.criterion: A randomized study in the case's population, controlled with placebo or vehicle, gives preliminary evidence of effectiveness, a greater hair count with the medicine than with control (P < 0.05), and reports short-term adverse effects. An uncontrolled study, or a controlled study without a significant difference in hair count, is partial.
milestones.set_by: FDA, 21 CFR 312.21(b)–(c), controlled efficacy studies and the prerequisite for expanded clinical trials.
milestones.threshold_quote: preliminary evidence suggesting effectiveness of the drug has been obtained

milestones.title: Expanded trials establish a medicine's benefit–risk profile for treating pattern hair loss.
milestones.criterion: Expanded randomized, double-blind trials in the case's population, controlled with placebo or vehicle, show a greater target-area hair count with the medicine than with control and report adverse events, in the numbers needed to evaluate benefit and risk and to write prescribing information. A trial that is single-blind, compares two active treatments only, or extends treatment without a control group is partial.
milestones.set_by: FDA, Drug Development and Review Definitions, Phase 3 Clinical Studies.
milestones.threshold_quote: evaluate the overall benefit-risk relationship of the drug.

not_found: No FDA or society document located specified a universal minimum hair-count gain or a mandatory one-year trial for androgenetic alopecia medicines.
The original minoxidil hair-loss IND clearance and its complete supporting toxicology package were not located.

results.finding: Minoxidil nonclinical safety studies (sample sizes unreported) found no special human hazards; no quantified follicle pharmacology result is reported.
results.detail: The source reports toxicology findings but no animal or in vitro experiment demonstrating an effect on hair follicles. Its general mechanism description does not supply that missing evidence.
results.quote: Preclinical data reveal no special hazards for humans based on conventional studies of safety pharmacology, repeated dose toxicity, genotoxicity or carcinogenic potential.

results.finding: Women received 5% minoxidil foam once daily in clinical research: 200 active-treated participants in the vehicle-controlled trial.
results.detail: Treatment lasted 24 weeks. The SmPC specifies a 1 g daily dose and reports clinical-trial adverse reactions, including headache and hypertrichosis; safety frequencies pool multiple trials.
results.quote: In a randomised, controlled, double-blind, multi-centre study, 5 % Minoxidil Topical Foam ONCE A DAY (MTF OD) was compared to a foam vehicle containing no active product. Each was applied once daily, for 24 weeks.

results.finding: In 397 women, once-daily 5% minoxidil foam increased target-area hair count over vehicle by 9.1 hairs/cm² at 24 weeks (p<0.0001).
results.detail: Randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled study; 200 received minoxidil and 197 vehicle. Clinical-trial adverse reactions are reported in pooled safety data.
results.quote:

results.finding: A phase 3 trial in 397 women found 5% minoxidil foam superior to vehicle by 9.1 hairs/cm² in the target area at 24 weeks.
results.detail: The multicentre trial was randomized and double-blind, with a defined 1 cm² target area. The prescribing information reports pooled trial safety findings. The additional evaluator-blind active-comparator study does not independently meet this criterion.

results.finding: Topical minoxidil at 3% was studied for efficacy and safety in 25 women with female androgenetic alopecia.
results.detail: The text establishes clinical study in the specified population and reports concentration and sample size, but does not report application dose or frequency or observed adverse events.
results.quote: To investigate the usefulness of topical minoxidil therapy in female androgenetic alopecia, we studied the efficacy and safety of 3% topical minoxidil in 25 affected women.

results.finding: Topical minoxidil at 2% or 3% was administered in clinical research with 126 male completers.
results.detail: The text reports concentrations and the total number completing the trial, but not adverse events or treatment-arm counts.
results.quote: One-hundred twenty-six healthy men with early male pattern baldness completed a 12-month double-blind, controlled trial of 2% and 3% topical minoxidil.

results.finding: In a randomized trial with 126 male completers, topical minoxidil significantly increased target-area terminal hair growth versus placebo at 4 months.
results.detail: The text describes target-area hair counting and statistical significance, but gives no explicit P value or significance threshold and reports no short-term adverse effects.
results.quote: Treatment of subjects with topical minoxidil for 4 months resulted in a statistically significant increase in terminal hair growth in comparison with placebo therapy.

results.finding: Among 126 men completing the 12-month minoxidil trial, none had net hair loss in the target area.
results.detail: The placebo group crossed to active treatment after 4 months, leaving the extension without a placebo control. Adverse events and evidence sufficient to establish the benefit–risk profile are not reported.
results.quote: No subject had a net hair loss in the target area during the study.

results.finding: In a randomized study of 28 women, participants applied 2% topical minoxidil or vehicle twice daily.
results.detail: Human administration and dose are reported, but the number receiving minoxidil and observed adverse events are not provided.
results.quote: Twenty-eight women with mild to moderate androgenetic alopecia were randomly assigned to apply either 2 percent topical minoxidil or placebo (vehicle) to their involved scalp areas twice daily.

results.finding: In 28 women randomized to minoxidil or vehicle, nonvellus target-area hair counts favored minoxidil at 32 weeks (p = 0.006).
results.detail: The randomized vehicle-controlled study reports a significant hair-count benefit, but does not report short-term adverse effects.
results.quote: At the end of thirty-two weeks, there was a statistically significant increase of nonvellus target area hairs in the minoxidil-treated versus the vehicle-treated group (p = 0.006).

results.finding: Minoxidil was administered to 113 women; 3 serious adverse events occurred, none related to study medication.
results.detail: Women received 5% foam once daily (56 participants; 50 mg/day) or 2% solution twice daily (57 participants; 40 mg/day) for 24 weeks, with scheduled safety assessments and adverse-event reporting.
results.quote:
Three serious AEs were reported, none of which
was related to study medication but one led to study
discontinuation.

results.finding: In 113 women, the difference in target-area hair-count gains between minoxidil foam and solution was nonsignificant (P = .441).
results.detail: The randomized 24-week study compared two active treatments without placebo or vehicle. Hair-count gains were 31.9 versus 28.4 hairs/cm²; short-term adverse effects were reported. Noninferiority does not satisfy the required superiority over placebo or vehicle.
results.quote:

this difference was not significant (P = .441).

results.finding: In 113 women, minoxidil foam met the hair-count noninferiority margin of 7.5 hairs/cm² versus minoxidil solution.
results.detail: This phase III trial reported target-area hair counts and adverse events over 24 weeks, but was single-blind, conducted at one site, and compared active treatments only. It therefore does not meet the double-blind, placebo- or vehicle-controlled criterion.
results.quote:
With a margin of noninferiority
of 7.5 hairs/cm2 a significant noninferiority of the 5%
MTF could be determined.

results.finding: Oral finasteride 1 mg/day was administered to 779 men in monitored trials enrolling 1553 men.
results.detail: Clinic visits occurred every 3 months, with laboratory monitoring and adverse-event collection. Sexual adverse events occurred in 4.2% receiving finasteride versus 2.2% receiving placebo.
results.quote:
Methods: In two 1-year trials, 1553 men (18 to 41 years of age) with male pattern hair loss
received oral finasteride 1 mg/d or placebo, and 1215 men continued in blinded extension
studies for a second year.

results.finding: In randomized trials enrolling 1553 men, finasteride increased target-area hair count by 107 hairs versus placebo at 1 year (P < .001).
results.detail: Two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled studies measured hair counts in a defined 5.1 cm² vertex area and reported adverse effects.
results.quote:

decrease of –21 ± 3.4 hairs (–2.7% ± 0.5%) for
placebo, and a difference of 107 ± 4.4 hairs (14%
± 0.6%) between groups (all P values < .001).

results.finding: Phase III finasteride trials enrolled 1553 men; 1215 entered blinded extensions, with a 138-hair advantage over placebo at 2 years.
results.detail: Replicate multicenter randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials established target-area hair-count benefit and reported clinical, laboratory and sexual adverse events over 2 years.
results.quote:
The difference between groups ( P < .001)
was 138 ± 16 hairs (16% ± 2.1%), which was sig-
nificantly greater ( P < .05) than the difference at
month 12.

results.finding: Finasteride 1 mg/day was studied in 1,553 randomized men; 1,215 continued into extension studies.
results.detail: Human administration and dose are reported, but the finasteride-treated number is not separated from placebo. Safety is summarized as generally well tolerated, without reporting specific adverse events observed.
results.quote: In two 1-year, Phase III trials, 1,553 men with MPHL were randomized to receive finasteride 1 mg/day or placebo, and 1,215 men continued in up to four 1-year, placebo-controlled extension studies.

results.finding: Finasteride improved hair outcomes versus placebo over 5 years in studies enrolling 1,553 men, with 1,215 entering extensions.
results.detail: Expanded randomized, placebo-controlled studies report durable efficacy across endpoints including hair counts. The text does not establish double blinding or a defined target area, and provides only a general safety summary. The significance notation is malformed as supplied.
results.quote: Treatment with finasteride led to durable improvements in scalp hair over five years (p 3/4 0.001 versus placebo, all endpoints), while treatment with placebo led to progressive hair loss.

results.finding: Topical minoxidil: 307 women received active treatment among 381 participants, applying 2 mL daily under clinical monitoring.
results.detail: Women received 5% minoxidil (153), 2% minoxidil (154), or placebo (74) for 48 weeks. Safety assessments documented dermatologic and cardiovascular adverse events, headaches, and withdrawals.
results.quote:
Patients applied 1 mL of assigned solution twice
daily at approximately 12-hour intervals (total daily
dose of 2 mL) for 48 weeks.

results.finding: Topical minoxidil: in 381 randomized women, both concentrations increased target-area hair counts versus placebo at 48 weeks (P < 0.001).
results.detail: Randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled study; 261 women were efficacy-evaluable. Adverse effects included pruritus, irritation, and hypertrichosis.

results.finding: Topical minoxidil: 381 women randomized; 5% treatment increased hair count by 24.5 hairs/cm² at 48 weeks, versus 9.4 with placebo.
results.detail: Nine-site, 48-week double-blind trial evaluated both concentrations against vehicle, with safety analyses in all 381 participants. Dermatologic adverse events were more frequent with 5%. Approximately 30% attrition and efficacy analyses restricted to evaluable patients limit interpretation.

results.finding: Topical minoxidil, tested at up to 5% in 18 stump-tailed macaques, enlarged vellus follicles toward terminal size.
results.detail: Animal follicle pharmacology supports hair-growth activity, but no toxicology results establish reasonably safe human testing. Indexing includes female animals; outcomes are not separated by sex or specifically linked to female pattern hair loss.
results.quote: minoxidil induces the enlargement of vellus follicles to the size of middle to terminal follicles (regrowth of hair effect)

results.finding: Finasteride toxicology in male rats (sample size unstated) found no tumorigenic effect during 24 months.
results.detail: Animal toxicology is reported, but no animal or in vitro result demonstrates an effect on hair follicles. Scalp enzyme-binding studies do not establish follicle effects or safety for a proposed human investigation.
results.quote:
No evidence of a tumorigenic effect was observed in a 24-month study in Sprague-Dawley rats receiving doses of 
finasteride up to 160 mg/kg/day in males and 320 mg/kg/day in females.

results.finding: Finasteride toxicology in female rats (sample size unstated) found no tumorigenic effect during 24 months.
results.detail: Animal toxicology is reported, including developmental toxicity elsewhere in the label. No nonclinical follicle-effect result or conclusion supporting reasonably safe investigation in women is supplied.
results.quote:
No evidence of a tumorigenic effect was observed in a 24-month study in Sprague-Dawley rats receiving doses of 
finasteride up to 160 mg/kg/day in males and 320 mg/kg/day in females.

results.finding: Finasteride clinical research treated 945 men; 1.4% discontinued because of drug-related adverse experiences.
results.detail: Three controlled trials administered finasteride 1 mg daily for 12 months; the label reports specific sexual adverse events and placebo comparisons.
results.quote:
In three controlled clinical trials for PROPECIA of 12-month duration, 1.4% of patients taking PROPECIA (n=945) 
were discontinued due to adve rse experiences that were considered to be possibly, probably or definitely drug-
related (1.6% for placebo; n=934).

results.finding: Finasteride was administered to 67 of 137 postmenopausal women in clinical research lasting 12 months.
results.detail: The study reports treated and control numbers, but no adverse events observed in the women. The product dose is specified elsewhere; the women's study paragraph does not explicitly state its dosing regimen.
results.quote:
In a study involving 137 postmenopausal women with androgenetic alopecia who were treated with PROPECIA 
(n=67) or placebo (n=70) for 12 months, effectiveness c ould not be demonstrated.

results.finding: Finasteride produced 107 more target-area hairs than placebo at 12 months in 1,351 assessed men (p<0.001).
results.detail: The vertex trials were randomized, double-blind and placebo-controlled. The label also reports adverse events during the first treatment year.
results.quote:
At 12 months there was a 107-hair difference from placebo (p<0. 001, PROPECIA [n =679] vs placebo 
[n=672]) within a 1-inch diameter circle (5.1 cm 2).

results.finding: In 137 postmenopausal women, finasteride showed no hair-count improvement over placebo after 12 months.
results.detail: The controlled study did not demonstrate efficacy. Randomization and short-term adverse effects in women are not reported in the supplied text.
results.quote:
In a study involving 137 postmenopausal women with androgenetic alopecia who were treated with PROPECIA 
(n=67) or placebo (n=70) for 12 months, effectiveness c ould not be demonstrated.

results.finding: Three trials enrolled 1,879 men; the vertex studies found a 107-hair target-area advantage over placebo at 12 months.
results.detail: Expanded randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials evaluated efficacy and safety. Safety data cover 945 finasteride-treated and 934 placebo-treated men; the vertex hair-count analysis included 679 and 672, respectively.
results.quote:
At 12 months there was a 107-hair difference from placebo (p<0. 001, PROPECIA [n =679] vs placebo 
[n=672]) within a 1-inch diameter circle (5.1 cm 2).

results.finding: A placebo-controlled finasteride study in 137 postmenopausal women failed to demonstrate effectiveness at 12 months.
results.detail: No greater hair count was demonstrated. The supplied account does not establish expanded randomized, double-blind trials or report women's adverse-event results sufficient to establish benefit–risk.
results.quote:
In a study involving 137 postmenopausal women with androgenetic alopecia who were treated with PROPECIA 
(n=67) or placebo (n=70) for 12 months, effectiveness c ould not be demonstrated.

results.finding: FDA labeling establishes finasteride's male-pattern-hair-loss indication; trials enrolled 1,879 men and showed a 107-hair advantage.
results.detail: The official label reports randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials and greater hair count in a defined scalp area. It does not establish the date or chronological priority of this indication's approval; the stated initial U.S. approval year is not identified as its hair-loss approval year.
results.quote: PROPECIA® is indicated for the treatment of male pattern hair loss (androgenetic alopecia) in MEN ONLY.
